### MAP-011C785E0E

- mapping source: [packages/uta-protocol/src/types/git.ts:296-306](../../../../packages/uta-protocol/src/types/git.ts#L296-L306)
- symbol: StageClosePositionParams
- unique targetChapters: 3, 5, 8, 9, 10, 14, 17, 19
- id: MAP-011C785E0E
- assessment: designed
- contractDisposition: retained
- contractRationale: Full versus exact close, scoped exposure and no-blind-retry remain a controlled effect contract; the provider may simply not declare a close leaf.
- contractAnchors:
  - [K02](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K04](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K08](../composition-contract.md)
- sourceEvidence:
  - packages/uta-protocol/src/types/git.ts:296-306: StageClosePositionParams carries aliceId/symbol, optional positive qty, optional subAccountId; empty qty means full close.
  - services/uta/src/domain/trading/UnifiedTradingAccount.ts:742-766: stageClose resolves Contract, parses positive Decimal qty when present, validates scope, and emits closePosition with Decimal quantity but no scope.
- currentBehavior: Close resolves a native contract and supports partial/full close; invalid quantity throws a generic Error and wallet scope is only transient.
- problem: A bare instrument/optional quantity cannot bind the exposure snapshot, account scope, multiplier, or current position version; full close is encoded as absence and generic errors lose typed reason.
- targetModel: Define `ClosePositionCommand { scope: AccountScope; target: InstrumentId; quantity: All | Exact(Quantity); expectedExposure: ExposureVersion }`. `All` is a tagged variant; risk admission remains a controlled-effect policy input rather than an untyped command field. Prepare stores exposure before-image, target quantity, multiplier/currency, and scope; dispatch/observation returns remaining exposure.
- pureTransitions:
  - decodeClose(input) -&gt; Result&lt;ClosePositionCommand, ValidationIssue&gt;; empty maps to All only at explicit boundary.
  - resolveClose(command, exposure) -&gt; Result&lt;ResolvedClose, PreconditionFailure&gt;; exact quantity &lt;= available and units match.
  - compileClose(resolved, capability) -&gt; Result&lt;NativeClosePlan, CapabilityFailure&gt;.
- effectBoundary: Application reads scoped exposure; pure validation/compiler; adapter dispatches close order. Writer persists exposure precondition and result.
- durability: Persist AccountScope, InstrumentId, quantity variant, expected exposure version, and observation/fill evidence. Full close does not mean target remains zero after external activity; criterion observes actual remainder.
- errors:
  - InvalidQuantity -&gt; ValidationIssue.
  - ScopeDiscoveryPending/Required/Mismatch -&gt; ScopeFailure.
  - ExposureChanged -&gt; PreconditionFailed/ReprepareRequired.
  - CloseUnsupported -&gt; CapabilityUnavailable.
  - UnknownOutcome -&gt; RecoveryRequired; no repeat close.
- preservedBehavior:
  - Preserve full-close default and positive partial quantity.
  - Correct absence-as-meaning, generic Error, and message-only subaccount.
  - Preserve partial close against latest position only with versioned scoped exposure evidence.
- replacementSteps:
  - Migrate stage/client/UnifiedTradingAccount close path.
  - Add All|Exact codec and exposure before-image/criterion.
  - Remove native Decimal/Contract from command.
- verificationCases:
  - Close All with exposure changed before dispatch fails precondition.
  - Exact quantity with multiplier is unit-validated.
  - Unknown close dispatch does not issue a second close blindly.
- openQuestions: —
- review: accepted — Accepted after repair: git.ts:296-306 and UnifiedTradingAccount.ts:742-766 encode full close as absent quantity, resolve a native contract, and retain wallet scope only transiently. The final ClosePositionCommand makes AccountScope, InstrumentId, All|Exact quantity, and ExposureVersion explicit; risk admission stays policy-bound, and a post-send Unknown never repeats the close (MAP-011C785E0E; K02-K04/K07-K12).

### MAP-02219D5749

- mapping source: [packages/uta-protocol/src/types/manager.ts:21-37](../../../../packages/uta-protocol/src/types/manager.ts#L21-L37)
- symbol: AggregatedEquity
- unique targetChapters: 3, 6, 7, 10, 13, 14, 19
- id: MAP-02219D5749
- assessment: designed
- contractDisposition: reframed
- contractRationale: Equity aggregation preserves FX/precision and missing-account evidence as data projections; unavailable inputs are not turned into transaction failures or zero balances.
- contractAnchors:
  - [K04](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K05](../composition-contract.md)
- sourceEvidence:
  - packages/uta-protocol/src/types/manager.ts:21-37: AggregatedEquity sums total equity/cash/PnL as strings, optional fxWarnings, and account rows with raw id/currency/health; no scope/freshness/status variant.
  - services/uta/src/domain/trading/uta-manager.ts:205-268: manager skips keyless accounts, defaults missing baseCurrency to USD and missing info to zero values, converts non-USD through optional FxService, and collects warning strings.
- currentBehavior: Manager concurrently reads healthy UTAs, excludes keyless accounts, converts non-USD values when FxService exists, and emits zero/USD rows for unavailable account info.
- problem: Default USD/zero values look like real balances, FX warnings are free text, and totals can mix stale/unknown/missing currencies. Per-account scope, valuation source/asOf, and confidence are absent.
- targetModel: Define `AccountEquityRow = IncludedAccount{scope: AccountScope; sourceCurrency: CurrencyAvailability; valuation: Valued{amounts: MoneyTotals; fx: FxEvidence} | Unvalued{reason; health; freshness}} | ExcludedAccount{providerId: ProviderId; reason: DataOnly|ScopeUnavailable; observedAt; sourceSequence}`, `CurrencyAvailability = Known(CurrencyCode)|Unknown(reason)`, `MoneyTotals { equity: Money; cash: Money; unrealizedPnL: Money; realizedPnL: Money }`, and `AggregatedEquityView { reportingCurrency: CurrencyCode; totals: CompleteTotals{amounts: MoneyTotals; sourceSequence}|PartialTotals{amounts: MoneyTotals; missing: ScopeReason[]}|UnavailableTotals{reason}; accounts: AccountEquityRow[]; fx: FxEvidence[]; completeness: Complete|Partial|Unavailable; asOf; sourceSequence }`. Keyless/data-only accounts use ExcludedAccount with explicit provider identity, never USD/zero.
- pureTransitions:
  - aggregateEquity(accounts, fxFacts, policy) -&gt; Result&lt;AggregatedEquityView, AggregationFailure&gt;; require reporting currency and fresh FX for every included converted amount.
  - classifyAccount(info, health) -&gt; Valued|Unvalued|Excluded(reason); no default currency or amount.
  - dedupeFxWarnings(evidence) -&gt; FxEvidence[]; structured evidence replaces free-text warnings.
- effectBoundary: Application queries account/FX services; pure Money/FX fold; protocol encodes projection. Missing info is not fabricated.
- durability: Persist per-account valuation and FX observation identities/validity windows; aggregate checkpoint records completeness and source sequence. Total is unavailable/partial when evidence insufficient.
- errors:
  - FxMissing/Stale -&gt; Unvalued account and Partial/Unavailable total.
  - CurrencyUnknown -&gt; Unvalued/Partial when the account remains observable; no default currency or fabricated total.
  - AccountOffline -&gt; row with Unvalued/health, not zeros.
  - NonPositive/invalid amount -&gt; ObservationFailure.
- preservedBehavior:
  - Preserve keyless exclusion, Decimal precision, FX conversion and warning visibility.
  - Correct USD/zero fallback and free-text warning by explicit valuation/completeness ADT.
- replacementSteps:
  - Migrate `getAggregatedEquity` and route/client output.
  - Use CurrencyCode/Money/FxObservation projections and structured warnings.
  - Delete optional fxWarnings/string account row fields.
- verificationCases:
  - An offline account appears Unvalued and cannot increase totals.
  - Missing FX prevents a Complete converted total and retains the source account amount as Unvalued.
  - All USD healthy accounts yield CompleteTotals with exact decimal strings.
  - A keyless UTA is marked Excluded(DataOnly), not a zero account.
- openQuestions: —
- review: accepted — Accepted after repair: manager.ts:21-37 and uta-manager.ts:205-268 default missing base currency to USD, missing info to zero, skip keyless accounts, and retain only free-text FX warnings. The final equity view uses explicit included/unvalued/excluded rows, CurrencyAvailability, FX evidence, completeness, and partial/unavailable totals; keyless/data-only is never a fabricated balance (MAP-02219D5749; K02-K05/K07/K08/K11).

### MAP-0422181E7C

- mapping source: [packages/uta-protocol/src/types/broker.ts:248-262](../../../../packages/uta-protocol/src/types/broker.ts#L248-L262)
- symbol: AccountInfo
- unique targetChapters: 5, 6, 10, 14, 19
- id: MAP-0422181E7C
- assessment: designed
- contractDisposition: reframed
- contractRationale: Account valuation retains decimal and same-currency evidence while becoming an immutable scoped observation; unavailable fields are not order failures or fabricated zeroes.
- contractAnchors:
  - [K04](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K05](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K08](../composition-contract.md)
- sourceEvidence:
  - packages/uta-protocol/src/types/broker.ts:248-262: AccountInfo stores baseCurrency and monetary fields as raw strings, optional margin/PnL fields, and numeric dayTradesRemaining without AccountScope.
  - services/uta/src/domain/trading/UnifiedTradingAccount.ts:1005-1023: getAccount mutates broker AccountInfo.unrealizedPnL after summing same-currency positions.
- currentBehavior: Account reads are mutable broker-shaped values; optional fields and base currency are interpreted by UTA aggregation, which can fall back to the broker number when currencies differ.
- problem: Raw strings do not establish currency/unit validity, and optional absent values have no reason/provenance. Mutation after the broker call hides whether PnL is broker-reported or locally derived; no sequence/freshness/scoped account identity is present.
- targetModel: Define `AccountSnapshot { scope: AccountScope; valuation: { currency: CurrencyAvailability; equity: MoneyAvailability; cash: MoneyAvailability; unrealizedPnL: MoneyAvailability; realizedPnL: MoneyAvailability }; buyingPower: MoneyAvailability; margin: MarginAvailability; dayTrades: DayTradeAvailability; valuationSource: BrokerReported{observationId}|DerivedFromExposures{inputSequence,formulaVersion}|Uncertain{reason}; observedAt: Instant; sequence: ObservationSequence; freshness: Fresh|Stale|Unknown }`. `CurrencyAvailability = Known(CurrencyCode)|Unknown(reason)`, `MoneyAvailability = Present(Money)|Unpriced{amount: DecimalString; reason}|Unavailable(reason)`, `MarginAvailability = Present{initial: MoneyAvailability; maintenance: MoneyAvailability}|Unavailable(reason)`, and `DayTradeAvailability = Present(NonNegativeInt)|Unavailable(reason)`; absent source fields or currencies are never implicit zero/USD.
- pureTransitions:
  - decodeAccount(raw, scope) -&gt; Result&lt;AccountSnapshot, ObservationFailure&gt;; validate each present Money currency/decimal and retain missing currency as Unpriced/Unknown valuation evidence.
  - deriveUnrealized(account, exposures, fx) -&gt; Result&lt;AccountValuation, ValuationUncertainty&gt;; do not mutate the broker snapshot.
  - mergeAccountObservation(previous, next) -&gt; latest by sequence/observation identity; out-of-order facts remain recorded but do not regress the projection.
- effectBoundary: Adapter decodes account data; application obtains positions/FX observations; pure accounting derives PnL; projection/API encodes a read-only snapshot.
- durability: Persist account observation and derived valuation provenance separately or atomically with a source sequence. AccountScope is part of every row/key; stale/fx-uncertain snapshots remain queryable with explicit status.
- errors:
  - InvalidAmountOrKnownCurrency -&gt; ObservationFailure.
  - MissingCurrency -&gt; retain Unpriced/Unknown valuation evidence; never default currency.
  - MixedCurrencyWithoutFx -&gt; ValuationUncertainty and per-currency breakdown.
  - AccountScopeUnknown -&gt; DiscoveryNotReady, never default account.
  - CapabilityAbsent(field) -&gt; field-level Unavailable, not zero.
  - ObservationOutOfOrder -&gt; ignore for projection and record duplicate evidence.
- preservedBehavior:
  - Preserve decimal precision and derived same-currency PnL invariant.
  - Correct in-place mutation and silent broker fallback by encoding valuationSource and uncertainty.
- replacementSteps:
  - Migrate manager aggregation and account routes to AccountSnapshot.
  - Replace optional string arithmetic with Money constructors and FX service facts.
  - Delete AccountInfo once all broker adapters and projections emit normalized snapshots.
- verificationCases:
  - Read all positions in base currency and observe DerivedFromExposures PnL equal to the fold.
  - Read mixed currencies without FX and observe Uncertain valuation plus broker source evidence, not a blind sum.
  - Read an account without day-trades support and observe DayTradeAvailability.Unavailable, not zero.
- openQuestions: —
- review: accepted — Accepted after repair: broker.ts:248-262 uses raw optional account fields and UnifiedTradingAccount.ts:1005-1023 mutates broker PnL after reading positions. The final AccountSnapshot carries scoped typed money/valuation availability and provenance; missing currency becomes Unpriced/Unknown rather than USD/zero, and derivation is an immutable projection (MAP-0422181E7C; K02-K05/K07/K08/K11).

### MAP-0647BF0194

- mapping source: [packages/uta-protocol/src/types/broker.ts:452-466](../../../../packages/uta-protocol/src/types/broker.ts#L452-L466)
- symbol: BrokerConfigField
- unique targetChapters: 3, 7, 9, 14, 15, 19
- id: MAP-0647BF0194
- assessment: designed
- contractDisposition: reframed
- contractRationale: Dynamic config remains schema-first and secret-safe, but fields are provider-declared capability leaves rather than a shared broker form interface with unknown defaults.
- contractAnchors:
  - [K01](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K03](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K07](../composition-contract.md)
- sourceEvidence:
  - packages/uta-protocol/src/types/broker.ts:452-466: BrokerConfigField uses primitive type labels, optional unknown default, string option tuples, description, and sensitive flag.
- currentBehavior: Frontend renders dynamic broker forms from an unvalidated descriptor; `default?: unknown` can contain arbitrary values and sensitive only describes masking.
- problem: The descriptor is a public config/schema boundary with no parser, constraints, secret reference semantics, or distinction between UI default and actual persisted secret. An unknown default can leak or produce invalid config.
- targetModel: Define serializable `ConfigFieldSpec` variants with named fields: `TextField{id,label,default: Default&lt;TextValue&gt;,constraints}`, `PasswordField{id,label,credential: CredentialRefRequirement}`, `NumberField{id,label,default: Default&lt;DecimalString&gt;,constraints}`, `BooleanField{id,label,default: Default&lt;boolean&gt;}`, and `SelectField{id,label,options: NonEmptyArray&lt;SelectOption&gt;,default: Default&lt;SelectValue&gt;}`. These are common projections only; provider-declared exact config extensions may add their own schema. `Default&lt;T&gt; = NoDefault | Value(T)`; `secret` is represented only by PasswordField and accepts CredentialRef, never plaintext. Field schema identity/version ties to the broker preset; UI projections never return secret values.
- pureTransitions:
  - decodeConfigField(raw) -&gt; Result&lt;ConfigFieldSpec, ProtocolViolation&gt;; default type must match variant.
  - validateConfig(form, schema) -&gt; Result&lt;NonSecretBrokerConfig, ConfigFailure&gt;; secret fields resolve to CredentialRef, not plaintext.
  - projectConfigForUi(config) -&gt; RedactedConfigView.
- effectBoundary: Protocol/config codec is pure. Application loads config and CredentialProvider injects secrets only into adapter scope; UI sees schema/redacted values.
- durability: Persist schema version, non-secret config, and secret reference ID; never include `default: unknown` or secret material in journal/plan/digest.
- errors:
  - ConfigShapeInvalid -&gt; ProtocolViolation.
  - RequiredFieldMissing/ConstraintViolation -&gt; ConfigFailure.
  - SecretValueExposed -&gt; RedactionFailure and abort response.
  - SchemaVersionMismatch -&gt; ReconfigureRequired.
- preservedBehavior:
  - Preserve dynamic form generation, option labels, and sensitive masking intent.
  - Correct unknown defaults and accidental secret flow by typed variants and CredentialRef.
- replacementSteps:
  - Replace `BrokerConfigField` with schema-driven ConfigFieldSpec.
  - Migrate preset/UI consumers to decode and validate values.
  - Keep adapter config schema authoritative; remove plain `unknown` defaults.
- verificationCases:
  - A number field with string default is rejected.
  - A password field response contains no value but includes CredentialRef requirement.
  - Unknown option submitted yields ConfigFailure before adapter creation.
- openQuestions: —
- review: accepted — Accepted after repair: broker.ts:452-466 gives config fields an unknown default and a masking-only sensitive flag. The final target uses typed field variants, matching Default&lt;T&gt;, CredentialRef for passwords, and provider-defined config extensions; UI/projection schemas never carry plaintext secrets (MAP-0647BF0194; K01-K03/K06/K07/K11).

### MAP-0CEEC81F23

- mapping source: [packages/uta-protocol/src/types/git.ts:225-246](../../../../packages/uta-protocol/src/types/git.ts#L225-L246)
- symbol: SimulatePriceChangeResult
- unique targetChapters: 1, 5, 6, 10, 12, 14, 17, 18, 20
- id: MAP-0CEEC81F23
- assessment: designed
- contractDisposition: retained
- contractRationale: Simulation success/rejection/indeterminate distinctions remain valuable pure report semantics, with no order approval, compensation or broker dispatch implied.
- contractAnchors:
  - [K03](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K05](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K12](../composition-contract.md)
- sourceEvidence:
  - packages/uta-protocol/src/types/git.ts:225-246: SimulatePriceChangeResult has success boolean/error string, nested current/simulated states, and summary strings including worstCase.
  - services/uta/src/domain/trading/git/TradingGit.ts:753-897: simulator returns success=false with empty position arrays on parse error, success=true for no positions, computes equity/PnL deltas, and appends an explanatory derivative exclusion note to worstCase.
- currentBehavior: Success/error bag mixes failure and report; parse errors discard current positions, no-position case is success with zeros, and worstCase is a free-form string combining risk outcome and exclusions.
- problem: Callers cannot distinguish invalid input, stale valuation, no positions, excluded derivatives, or valid zero-impact simulation. Empty arrays on failure can be mistaken for no exposures; string summary cannot be machine-checked.
- targetModel: Define `SimulationReport = ValidReport({scope, scenario, sourceSequence, current, simulated, summary, exclusions, worstCase: WorstCaseAssessment}) | SimulationRejected({issues, sourceStateRef}) | SimulationIndeterminate({uncertainty, sourceStateRef})`. `WorstCaseAssessment` is ADT (LossEstimate|NoLoss|Unavailable) with Money/Ratio; keep human prose derived.
- pureTransitions:
  - simulateScenario(state, scenario) -&gt; Result&lt;SimulationReport, SimulationValidationFailure|SimulationIndeterminate&gt;; preserve source state reference on failure.
  - summarizeRisk(positionAfter[]) -&gt; WorstCaseAssessment; exclude rows structurally.
  - recomputeReport(inputDigest, snapshot) -&gt; deterministic same report.
- effectBoundary: Pure report builder; application reads Position/Account snapshots and encodes result. No broker calls or mutation.
- durability: Persist optional report with input digest/source sequence/calculation version, not as account state. A failure report must not masquerade as successful empty snapshot.
- errors:
  - InvalidScenario -&gt; SimulationRejected with issues.
  - NoPositions -&gt; ValidReport with EmptyExposure state (explicit), not generic zeros.
  - ValuationUncertain/Stale -&gt; SimulationIndeterminate.
  - WorstCaseUnavailable -&gt; typed summary state.
- preservedBehavior:
  - Preserve no-position successful report and derivative warning semantics.
  - Correct boolean/error bag, failure empty arrays, and free-form worstCase by explicit variants.
  - Retain exact equity/PnL deltas and multiplier math.
- replacementSteps:
  - Migrate simulator route/tools/UI to union result.
  - Add source-state reference and exclusions list.
  - Delete success/error fields from authority schema; derive text summary at presentation.
- verificationCases:
  - Malformed change returns Rejected while current snapshot reference remains available.
  - No positions returns EmptyExposure valid report.
  - Mixed-currency input yields Indeterminate not numeric aggregate.
  - Derivative exclusion appears in structured exclusions and derived worst-case text.
- openQuestions: —
- review: accepted — Accepted: git.ts:225-246 and TradingGit.ts:753-897 combine success/error, empty failure arrays, no-position success, and free-form worstCase text. The final SimulationReport distinguishes ValidReport, Rejected, and Indeterminate, models EmptyExposure and WorstCaseAssessment explicitly, and preserves source state on failure without treating emptiness as generic success (MAP-0CEEC81F23; K02/K03/K05/K08/K11).
- design: [design.md](design.md)

  - Add AccountScope/InstrumentId filters and event ranges.
  - Retire in-memory commit array log as authority.
- verificationCases:
  - Request limit 10 with more records and observe next cursor.
  - Filter two same-symbol instruments by InstrumentId and observe only requested scope.
  - Corrupt parent digest and observe AuditIntegrityFailure.

The final audit log adds canonical commit/event identities, cursor/filter-version pagination, scope/instrument filters, and explicit source sequence, keeping the log a projection rather than an unbounded array authority (MAP-18E2D21F66; K02/K03/K05/K08/K11).

- id: MAP-19CA6A1780
- assessment: designed

- contractRationale: Simulation selectors and Decimal arithmetic become a scoped pure data-unit contract; simulation never creates an order approval or dispatch effect.

- effectBoundary: Pure simulation parser/resolver/calculator. Application reads scoped PositionObservation and supplies now/request facts; no broker mutation or journal write.
- durability: A simulation request/result is an audit/query record with scope and input digest only if retained; never a trade action or dispatch job. Preserve exclusion reasons in result.
- errors:
  - InvalidChangeFormat -&gt; SimulationValidationFailure.
  - InstrumentAmbiguous/Unknown -&gt; QueryFailure.
  - NegativeResultPrice -&gt; SimulationValidationFailure.
  - ValuationUncertain -&gt; SimulationIndeterminate.
- preservedBehavior:
  - Preserve `all`, absolute/relative modes, multiplier-aware math, and loud derivative exclusion for underlying selectors.
  - Correct symbol/aliceId ambiguity and floating parse with scoped InstrumentId/DecimalString.
  - Keep simulation read-only.
- replacementSteps:
  - Migrate simulator routes/tools to scenario codec.
  - Resolve selectors via InstrumentId/catalog before invoking pure simulation.
  - Delete free-form PriceChangeInput once clients use tagged change variants.
- verificationCases:
  - @88000 retains exact decimal and rejects zero.
  - Relative change against derivative-specific InstrumentId updates only that position.
  - Underlying selector with option rows returns explicit excluded derivative list.
  - Unknown selector returns typed failure rather than unchanged all positions.
- openQuestions: —
- review: accepted — Accepted: git.ts:194-201 accepts free symbol/aliceId/all and absolute/relative strings, while TradingGit.ts:778-817 matches display symbols, parseFloats, and excludes derivatives after matching. - contractRationale: The observed loss of NOT_A_REAL_CODE remains an empirical defect; the correction is an open unknown-failure schema with provider mapping versions, not a new closed code list.
- contractAnchors:

  - [K08](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K11](../composition-contract.md)
- sourceEvidence:
  - packages/uta-protocol/src/types/broker.spec.ts:21-28: an unknown code NOT_A_REAL_CODE is passed as a BrokerError-like object and BrokerError.from silently returns code UNKNOWN.
- currentBehavior: The legacy parser accepts only its closed set and silently degrades an unrecognized structured code to UNKNOWN, losing the original code while retaining the Error message.
- problem: Silently replacing an adapter or venue code hides whether a new protocol version, capability rejection, or transport corruption caused the event. UNKNOWN also has no association or recovery rule, so a scheduler could retry unsafely.
- targetModel: Use `UnknownBrokerFailure { tag:"UnknownBrokerFailure"; rawCode: RedactedCode; category:"Unclassified"; retryability:"Unknown"; evidence; subject: ProviderInstance|AccountScoped{scope: AccountScope}; actionRef? }` for a syntactically valid but unmapped code, and `ProtocolViolation` for an invalid envelope. Unknown is a durable outcome requiring observation/operator policy, not an ordinary UNKNOWN broker code.
- pureTransitions:
  - mapNativeCode(code, message, mappingVersion) -&gt; Result&lt;BrokerFailure, MappingGap&gt;; preserve rawCode when mapping misses.
  - classifyRecovery(failure, attemptState) -&gt; ObserveUnknown | OperatorRequired, never QueueUnsent solely because the code is unknown.
- effectBoundary: The protocol parser is pure; an adapter supplies its versioned mapping table. Scheduler/application consumes the typed result and may issue an explicit observation job.
- durability: Persist rawCode as redacted evidence, mappingVersion, and the attempt/action identity in the event payload. Do not overwrite a previously unknown event when a newer mapping becomes available; projections may enrich separately.
- errors:
  - ProtocolViolation(invalidTagOrShape) -&gt; reject request before journal mutation.
  - UnknownBrokerFailure(code) -&gt; record and suspend automatic retry until observation/evidence or operator recovery.
  - CodeMappingUnavailable(version) -&gt; mark adapter capability degraded.
- preservedBehavior:
  - Keep the fact that unrecognized native codes cannot be trusted as a known code.
  - Intentionally change silent fallback to UNKNOWN into explicit unknown evidence, preventing false retry/terminal claims.
- replacementSteps:
  - Change the test expectation to assert rawCode preservation and UnknownBrokerFailure.
  - Add protocol-version/mappingVersion to pack boundary and recovery classifier.
  - Expose a stable redacted response while keeping native code out of user-facing messages where sensitive.
- verificationCases:
  - Pass NOT_A_REAL_CODE and observe rawCode retained, Unknown retryability, and no dispatch redispatch.
  - Pass malformed `code: 7` and observe ProtocolViolation rather than UnknownBrokerFailure.
- openQuestions: —
- review: accepted — Accepted after repair: broker.spec.ts:21-28 shows NOT_A_REAL_CODE silently collapsing to UNKNOWN. The final target preserves the redacted raw code and subject, emits UnknownBrokerFailure for an unmapped valid shape, and reserves ProtocolViolation for malformed input, preventing unsafe retry or terminal claims (MAP-1A43E0FCC4; K02/K03/K07/K08/K11).

The source order vocabulary is broader than the prior model: IBKR advertises MOC/LOC/REL, native Order carries REL-only percentOffset and OPG-capable tif fields, Alpaca maps OPG but does not advertise MOC/LOC/REL, Longbridge rejects OPG, and CCXT only directly maps MKT/LMT while the place path omits order.tif.
- problem: There is no prepared action, AccountScope, before-image/version, DispatchStarted write-ahead, idempotency identity, typed acknowledgement/observation, or explicit FailurePolicy. Partial order patches defer validation to SDK, MOC/LOC/REL and opening-auction intent are absent from the canonical union, and adapter-specific TIF/order-type behavior can silently fall through or drop fields.
- targetModel: Represent a controlled order effect as a transaction wrapper around a selected provider-declared input leaf. The leaf composes common semantic units (quantity/notional, price/distance, timing, relations and protection) with exact provider extension fields; local unions such as Units versus Notional, Amount versus Percent, and Keep/Set/Clear remain where they are true preconditions. Native MOC/LOC/REL/OPG facts from the cited IBKR sources are preserved as provider leaf metadata/parameters, not a cross-provider order-kind enumeration or mandatory handler. If a provider lacks a leaf, the capability tree omits it; if the leaf exists but is unavailable, the descriptor says so.   - classifyDispatchAck(step, rawEvidence) -&gt; Result&lt;Ack&lt;ActionTag&gt;, DispatchFailure&gt;; the effect interpreter supplies raw evidence after writer-persisted DispatchStarted.
  - classifyObservation(attempt, typedObservation) -&gt; RemoteOutcome&lt;ActionTag&gt;; criterion evaluator settles the durable state.
- effectBoundary: Only BrokerActionInterpreter performs native dispatch/observe IO and secret resolution, returning typed Ack/RemoteOutcome. Transaction application/writer owns prepare/approval, DispatchStarted write-ahead, jobs, and durable progress; protocol encodes records and never invokes the broker.
- durability: Writer atomically records command receipt, selected leaf payload/fingerprint, locks, DispatchStarted, ack/observation, and jobs. No result is returned as committed authority before SQL commit.
- errors:
  - DeclaredInputInvalid/CapabilityUnavailable -&gt; prepare rejection for the selected leaf.
  - ScopeRequired/ScopeMismatch -&gt; reject before prepare.
  - DispatchUnknown -&gt; Reconciling; no redispatch without evidence.
  - KnownBrokerRejection -&gt; ContinueOnKnownRejection only when plan policy says so.
  - Unknown -&gt; suspend remaining forward steps.
- preservedBehavior:
  - Preserve all current order terms and sequential per-operation execution for legacy independent batches, but make continuation explicit in FailurePolicy.
  - Correct direct Promise mutation, bool result, and Partial&lt;Order&gt; boundary.
  - Preserve accepted-but-working orders as non-filled.
  - Preserve IBKR MOC/LOC/REL and opening-auction requestability as exact provider-leaf evidence; adapters without that leaf or evidence return structural absence/Unavailable/Unknown rather than downgrading them.
- replacementSteps:
  - Introduce transaction-kernel action contracts and per-action adapter interpreters.
  - Migrate stage/commit/push routes and remove direct calls to IBroker mutation methods.
  - Translate legacy operation batches with explicit policy and retain scope/field relations in digest.
- verificationCases:
  - A known rejection in step 1 under ContinueOnKnownRejection lets step 2 proceed and records both outcomes.
  - Unknown timeout after step 1 suspends step 2.
  - A selected provider leaf either preserves its declared notional/trailing/protection extension in the prepared digest or returns CapabilityUnavailable, never silently dropping fields.
  - A provider-declared REL or OpeningAuction leaf retains its exact offset/cap/TIF parameters; a provider without that leaf receives no downgraded DAY request.

- review: accepted — Accepted after repair: broker.ts:524-529 directly mutates native order objects, while UnifiedTradingAccount.ts:603-637,703-715 and the IBKR/Alpaca/Longbridge/CCXT sources prove sizing, trailing, MOC/LOC/REL, OPG, and TIF differences. - contractRationale: Loose HTTP errors are replaced by route/action schemas with provider extension evidence and typed recovery; transport status remains presentation rather than universal retry policy.

  - [K03](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K07](../composition-contract.md)

- sourceEvidence:

  - packages/uta-protocol/src/client/UTAClient.ts:75-84: non-2xx bodies are read as unknown and converted to UTAHttpError using a generic `error` property/message.
- currentBehavior: Every endpoint is expected to return one loose error bag, while the client turns any body into a generic Error-like UTAHttpError; route/action context is not preserved.
- problem: The bag collapses TransactionFailure, QueryFailure, DispatchFailure, BrokerRejection, ProtocolViolation, authentication, and storage faults. `transient` is not enough to decide retry versus observation; `message` becomes the effective protocol and can leak secrets.
- targetModel: Replace with versioned route-specific `FailureEnvelope` variants: common cases include `TransportInvalid`, `AuthenticationFailed`, `AuthorizationDenied`, `DomainRejected` (named failure payload), `VersionConflict`, `StorageUnavailable`, `DispatchUnknown`, `ProtocolViolation`, and query/capability failures; a provider leaf may add exact error extensions. Each payload carries redacted stable code, scope/action/command identity where relevant, and evidence-bound retry/recovery disposition. Client decodes the selected route schema and exposes typed Result/exception wrappers by route.
- pureTransitions:
  - encodeFailure(failure) -&gt; FailureEnvelope; exhaustive mapping from domain variants.
  - decodeFailure(unknown) -&gt; Result&lt;ProtocolFailure, ProtocolViolation&gt;; reject generic `{error:string}` for new routes.
  - mapHttp(status, envelope) -&gt; TransportOutcome; status is presentation, not failure identity.
- effectBoundary: HTTP transport/application owns status and authentication; domain failures are constructed before encoding. No generic `Error.message` is consumed for retry/recovery.
- durability: Journal stores domain failure/event references and schema versions; HTTP response is a projection. Storage failure must not be collapsed into broker transient or retried mutation.
- errors:
  - ProtocolViolation -&gt; invalid request/pack protocol failure.
  - VersionConflict(scope, expected, observed) -&gt; caller reloads current transaction.
  - DispatchUnknown(identity) -&gt; query/recovery, no retry by HTTP client.
  - StorageUnavailable -&gt; report unavailable; no receipt claimed.
  - BrokerRejection -&gt; map action policy, not generic 500.
- preservedBehavior:
  - Preserve human-readable hint/message as redacted presentation text.
  - Correct universal wire shape and generic client exception by route-specific exhaustive codecs.
- replacementSteps:
  - Define schemas in `protocol/` and map all transaction/query/capability routes.
  - Migrate UTAClient to typed decoding and preserve status/body for diagnostics only.
  - Delete WireBrokerError and generic `error` property requirement.
- verificationCases:
  - Return known DomainRejected and observe caller can inspect variant/action/scope.
  - Return malformed body and observe ProtocolViolation, not UTAHttpError with opaque message.
  - Drop response after commit and re-query receipt without sending a second command.
- openQuestions: —
- review: accepted — Accepted: errors.ts:1-19 exposes one loose code/message/transient bag and UTAClient.ts:75-84 turns arbitrary non-2xx bodies into a generic error. - currentBehavior: AccountCapabilities exposes supportedSecTypes and supportedOrderTypes as unvalidated string arrays and optional historical bars; the source set includes IBKR MOC/LOC/REL, while adapter details and OPG handling are not normalized into capability decisions.
- problem: String labels do not say whether a named order kind/TIF is supported, rejected, or unknown for this scope and adapter, and cannot distinguish a static advertisement from executable native mapping.
- targetModel: Build a versioned `CapabilitySet` from provider-declared capability leaves. The fixed descriptor envelope carries capability identity, command path, schema versions/fingerprint, input/result/error schemas, delivery/effect metadata, resource requirements, provenance and `Supported|Unavailable|Unknown` availability. Each provider may declare only the order, query, data or identity leaves it implements; there is no cross-provider action map and no requirement that every provider implement every action. Transaction preparation pins the selected descriptor revision; authorization and policy remain separate.
- pureTransitions:
  - deriveActionAvailability(staticConfig, connection, scopeFacts) -&gt; CapabilitySet; separate static and current evidence.
  - checkDeclaredLeaf(action, capabilities, context) -&gt; Result&lt;void, CapabilityFailure&gt;; validate only the selected leaf schema and its declared relations.
  - compareFingerprint(prepared, current) -&gt; Same | ReprepareRequired.
- effectBoundary: Capability service performs discovery/refresh effects; protocol codec serializes capability view; transaction kernel only receives an immutable snapshot.
- durability: Persist capability revision/fingerprint with prepared plan and action evidence; stale capabilities cannot authorize dispatch.
- errors:
  - CapabilityUnavailable(action, reason) -&gt; caller changes plan.
  - CapabilityUnknown(action) -&gt; block rather than assume.
  - FingerprintChanged -&gt; ReprepareRequired.
  - ScopeMismatch -&gt; reject capability lookup.
- preservedBehavior:
  - Preserve secType/order labels for UI/catalog where evidence supports them.
  - Correct string-array static/synchronous API with action-specific, versioned availability.
- replacementSteps:
  - Migrate `IBroker.getCapabilities`, manager summaries, and broker pack manifests.
  - Add conformance evidence for each selected leaf's notional/trailing/protection relations without imposing them on other providers.
  - Delete AccountCapabilities legacy arrays after protocol views switch.
- verificationCases:
  - A provider snapshot declares a units-only leaf and a notional request is rejected by that leaf schema, without changing another provider.
  - A capability revision changes between prepare and dispatch and the selected leaf requires reprepare.
  - A read-only scope exposes a query leaf while an undeclared write leaf is absent rather than Unsupported-filled.
  - IBKR MOC/LOC/REL and OPG relations appear only in the provider descriptor that declares them; Alpaca/Longbridge/CCXT evidence remains unsupported or unknown where mapping is absent.
- openQuestions: —
- review: accepted — Accepted: broker.ts:445-450 exposes unvalidated string capability arrays, while IBKR, Alpaca, Longbridge, and CCXT sources show different MOC/LOC/REL/OPG/TIF support. The final CapabilitySet derives exact provider leaves and descriptors with Supported/Unavailable/Unknown availability and fingerprint pinning, rather than a cross-provider action map (MAP-46669371C2; K01-K04/K06-K08/K11).

- sourceEvidence:

  - services/uta/src/domain/trading/git/TradingGit.ts:969-976: mapOrderStatus converts native states to filled/cancelled/rejected/default submitted.
- currentBehavior: One status union is reused for placement, sync, cancel, external observation, and user rejection; unknown native state defaults to submitted.
- problem: The flat status cannot distinguish acknowledgement, working, partial fills, unknown outcome, recovery, or action-specific legal transitions. Mapping unknown native state to submitted can falsely claim a working order.
- targetModel: Use three distinct ADTs: `DispatchState = Planned|DispatchStarted|Acknowledged|Rejected|Unknown`; `OrderLifecycle = Working|PartiallyFilled|Filled|Cancelled|Expired|Rejected|Unknown`; and exact 12-state `TransactionState = Draft|Preparing|Prepared|AwaitingApproval|Queued|Executing|Reconciling|Aborting|Compensating|Committed|Compensated|RecoveryRequired`. `RecoveryRequired` carries a durable RecoveryCase owner/exclusion; UserRejected is a domain command outcome, not a broker order status.
- pureTransitions:
  - decodeNativeOrderState(raw) -&gt; Result&lt;OrderLifecycle, ObservationFailure&gt;; unknown status =&gt; Unknown.
  - evolveStep(state, Ack|Observation|Failure) -&gt; Result&lt;nextState, ReplayViolation&gt;; enforce action-specific legal transitions.
  - evaluateCriterion(criterion, observation) -&gt; Satisfied|Pending|Violated|Indeterminate.
- effectBoundary: Adapter maps native state; pure transaction evolution/projection maps statuses. Protocol encodes discriminated variants.
- durability: Persist lifecycle/dispatch/transaction transitions with source sequence and recovery-case ownership; duplicate observations are idempotent by broker identity and Unknown never becomes Rejected.
- errors:
  - UnknownNativeStatus -&gt; ObservationFailure/Unknown, not Submitted.
  - IllegalTransition -&gt; ReplayViolation.
  - PartialFill -&gt; Working with cumulative fill, not Filled.
  - UserRejected -&gt; DomainRejected with no dispatch.
- preservedBehavior:
  - Preserve filled/cancelled/rejected status presentation where confirmed.
  - Correct default-submitted mapping and status reuse by preserving unknown/partial/recovery distinctions.
- replacementSteps:
  - Migrate sync/history projections and action result codecs.
  - Add status/evolution exhaustive cases and remove flat casts.
  - Expose presentation labels separately from transaction state.
- verificationCases:
  - Native status PartiallyFilled remains partial and schedules observation.
  - Unknown status after dispatch is Unknown/Reconciling and retains the dispatch identity.
  - Cancel acknowledgement without terminal observation does not produce Cancelled.
  - RecoveryRequired retains its RecoveryCase owner and conflict exclusion.
- openQuestions: —
- review: accepted — Accepted: git.ts:56-58 has one flat status union and TradingGit.ts:969-976 maps unknown native states to submitted. The final separate DispatchState, OrderLifecycle, and local 12-state TransactionState preserves confirmed labels but represents partial/unknown/reconciling/recovery transitions without a false Submitted default (MAP-4B40267FF6; K02/K03/K07/K08/K11).

- assessment: designed

- sourceEvidence:
  - packages/uta-protocol/src/types/broker.ts:159-168: PlaceOrderLeg carries only a string orderId and takeProfit/stopLoss kind.
- currentBehavior: A placement result can list protective child IDs, allowing the Git scanner to treat legs as submitted and later synchronize them.
- problem: The leg ID has no AccountScope, parent relationship, native-id provenance, or child order terms; a bare string can collide across accounts and cannot prove which action created it.
- targetModel: Define `OrderLegRef { scope: AccountScope; parent: ScopedOrderRef; child: ScopedOrderRef; role: TakeProfit|StopLoss|ProviderDefinedLegRole{code; evidence}; protection: TakeProfitSpec|StopLossSpec|ProviderDefinedProtection{leaf; evidence}; group: GroupEvidence }`, where `GroupEvidence = ProvenAtomic{groupId,evidenceVersion}|RuntimeManaged{programId}|Unknown{reason}`. The parent acknowledgement returns `AttachedOrderLeg` records; each child remains independently observable and its identity cannot be reconstructed from a bare string.
- pureTransitions:
  - compileProtection(parentSpec, capability) -&gt; Result&lt;PreparedLegPlan[], CapabilityFailure&gt;; enforce TP/SL price relations and retain every child field.
  - associateLegObservation(parent, childObservation) -&gt; Result&lt;OrderLegState, ObservationFailure&gt;; dedupe by scoped child identity and require parent relation evidence.
  - pendingOrders(snapshot) -&gt; includes parent and legs while lifecycle is Working, PartiallyFilled, or Unknown; Unknown stays visible for recovery.
- effectBoundary: Pure relationship constructors live in domain. Adapter dispatch/observation supplies native child IDs and atomic-group evidence; projection encodes safe leg views.
- durability: Persist parent/child identity, role, action/attempt, and native group identity in the journal before exposing a leg as pending. A leg result cannot be reconstructed from a string alone.
- errors:
  - InvalidProtectionRelation(parent, child) -&gt; refuse prepare.
  - LegIdentityConflict(scope, child) -&gt; record observation conflict and stop automatic reconciliation.
  - NativeGroupUnknown -&gt; do not claim atomic bracket success.
- preservedBehavior:
  - Preserve tracking of bracket legs from birth and inclusion in pending-order scans.
  - Correct cross-account string collisions and false assumption that every venue creates a linked atomic group.
- replacementSteps:
  - Replace PlaceOrderLeg with scoped OrderLegRef and migrate TradingGit.getKnownOrderIds/getPendingOrderIds.
  - Map native bracket responses in each adapter to role/group evidence.
  - Project child rows from journal order graph.
- verificationCases:
  - Same child ID on two AccountScopes remains distinct.
  - A TP child observed without parent linkage is external/unknown, not silently attached.
  - A partial bracket response yields parent plus explicit missing-leg evidence.
- openQuestions: —
- review: accepted — Accepted after repair: broker.ts:159-168 exposes only a string child orderId and TP/SL kind. The final target adds scoped parent/child identities, provider-defined role/protection extensions, and ProvenAtomic/RuntimeManaged/Unknown group evidence; each leg remains independently observable, so a bare ID cannot imply a linked bracket (MAP-77D0297A77; K02/K04/K07/K08/K11).

- contractRationale: Catalog search/details/expand/refresh are independently declared query leaves, preserving cache and completeness evidence without mandatory methods or transaction state.

  - packages/uta-protocol/src/types/broker.ts:500-522: IBroker contract search methods return ContractDescription[]/native ContractDetails, optional expandContract returns ContractExpansion, and optional refreshCatalog Promise&lt;void&gt;.
- currentBehavior: Search/details/expansion and refresh are mixed in the broker object; optional methods signal unsupported behavior with undefined while refresh errors propagate and search returns native descriptions.
- problem: Undefined method and empty arrays conflate unsupported, unavailable, and no matches. Native ContractDescription crosses the catalog/query boundary; no catalog revision or freshness is carried.
- targetModel: Expose catalog behavior as independently declared query leaves (for example search, details, expansion or refresh) whose schemas and errors are derived from provider declarations. A provider without a leaf has structural absence; an existing leaf that is offline or unauthorized reports availability separately. Normalized results carry InstrumentId/descriptor, revision, cursor/completeness and asOf; catalog reads remain projections and never execution authority.

- effectBoundary: Application catalog service performs IO through adapter port; protocol codec encodes search/detail/expansion pages. `refresh` is supervised effect, not direct mutation from a domain object.
- durability: Persist catalog revision, source, completeness, and refresh outcome in projection/journal where required. Do not treat cache rows as execution authority without revision check.
- errors:
  - CapabilityUnavailable(CatalogAction) -&gt; explicit failure.
  - NoMatches -&gt; complete empty result, distinct from Partial/Unavailable.
  - CatalogStale -&gt; query may return stale view but prepare rejects stale identity.
  - InstrumentNotFound -&gt; QueryFailure.
- preservedBehavior:
  - Preserve hub/leaf expansion and keep cache on refresh failure.
  - Correct optional method/empty fallback and native descriptions by explicit capability/result variants.
- replacementSteps:

  - Add catalog revision to InstrumentRef/PreparedPlan identity evidence.
  - Delete native-return methods from IBroker.
- verificationCases:
  - Unsupported adapter returns CapabilityUnavailable, not []/undefined.
  - Refresh failure leaves prior revision with stale marker.
  - Partial catalog page exposes missing cursor/namespace evidence and cannot authorize write identity.
- openQuestions: —
- review: accepted — Accepted: broker.ts:500-522 mixes optional search/details/expand/refresh methods, native descriptions, undefined support, and empty results. The final independent query leaves distinguish structural absence, availability, no matches, completeness, revision, and freshness; catalog projections cannot authorize execution (MAP-781BB54D06; K01-K06/K07/K11).

  - toDisplayShortHash(id) -&gt; string; never parse display text back as authority.
- effectBoundary: Pure canonical encoder/digest/chain verifier; journal/export reader performs file/DB IO. No random/time hidden in hash.

- problem: The regex table is lossy and language/provider dependent. It can misclassify a new broker code, expose sensitive text, or label a post-dispatch timeout as retryable NETWORK.   - NativeMappingUnavailable(adapterVersion) -&gt; capability/evidence gap; block safe dispatch classification without claiming provider support.

- unique targetChapters: 3, 9, 14, 19
- id: MAP-D4DBF6173C
- assessment: designed
- contractDisposition: reframed
- contractRationale: The source confirms native SDK and Decimal leakage; the target keeps exact serializable protocol units but lets each provider own codecs and declared extensions.
- contractAnchors:
  - [K02](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K03](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K07](../composition-contract.md)
- sourceEvidence:
  - packages/uta-protocol/src/types/broker.ts:1-12: the public broker module imports Contract, Order, OrderState, Execution, OrderCancel, ContractDescription/Details from @traderalice/ibkr, Decimal from decimal.js, and side-effect imports contract-ext.
  - services/uta/src/domain/trading/brokers/types.ts:1-7: the service compatibility module re-exports the entire public protocol barrel into broker implementations.
- currentBehavior: The shared package is the source of both native SDK object types and Decimal-bearing values consumed by UTA and broker packs.
- problem: A package advertised as wire protocol can receive mutable SDK class instances, runtime Decimal objects, declaration augmentations, and broker-specific optional fields. This violates the public/kernel dependency direction and makes JSON/replay semantics depend on SDK constructors.
- targetModel: Split the shared boundary into serializable schema declarations for identities, semantic order/data units, observations, queries and projections. A provider pack supplies its own native Contract/Order/Execution/Decimal codecs and exact extension fields; static types, validators and metadata are derived from each declaration. The protocol package has no SDK constructors or universal action map, while durable effect records store validated descriptions only.
- pureTransitions:
  - decodeInstrumentRef(wire) -&gt; Result&lt;InstrumentId, IdentityFailure&gt;; decodeDeclaredInput(wire, providerLeaf) -&gt; Result&lt;ProviderInput, InputValidationFailure&gt;.
  - encodeNativeRequest(ResolvedAction, adapterFacts) -&gt; Result&lt;NativePlanRecord, DispatchFailure&gt; inside adapter; protocol never imports SDK constructors.
  - encodeProjection(nativeObservation) -&gt; normalized serializable view before projection/journal consumption.
- effectBoundary: No IO in protocol/domain codecs. Adapter layer owns SDK parsing and secret injection; application/effect services own fetching facts and journal writes.
- durability: Journal/event schemas store canonical encoded values plus encoding version, not SDK objects or Decimal instances. Projection rows use normalized codecs and can be rebuilt without loading a broker pack.
- errors:
  - ProtocolDependencyViolation(module) -&gt; fail package boundary/build gate.
  - InvalidDecimalString(field) / InvalidInstrumentIdentity -&gt; reject wire/domain construction.
  - PlanVersionUnsupported(adapterVersion) -&gt; refuse dispatch rather than reinterpret native data.
- preservedBehavior:
  - Preserve Decimal precision by encoding decimal strings and preserve native fields only as adapter metadata when evidence requires it.
  - Intentionally remove SDK objects from every public protocol type, including read projections.
- replacementSteps:
  - Replace imports and side-effect augmentation with protocol-local brands/codecs.
  - Create one native codec per adapter and migrate services/uta/src/domain/trading/brokers/types.ts callers to SPI interfaces.
  - Delete the compatibility barrel once all adapters/application code consume normalized contracts.
- verificationCases:
  - Attempt to serialize a native Contract/Decimal through a public response and observe schema rejection or normalized output with no constructor fields.
  - Load protocol package without any broker pack and observe all schemas/codecs remain usable.
- openQuestions: —
- review: accepted — Accepted: broker.ts:1-12 imports IBKR SDK classes, Decimal, and contract-ext while brokers/types.ts:1-7 re-exports the broad barrel. The final target moves native codecs and exact extensions into provider packs and leaves only schema-derived serializable values at the protocol boundary; replay stores encoded values, not SDK instances (MAP-D4DBF6173C; K01-K04/K07/K11).

### MAP-DC3A63D407

- symbol: AddResult
- unique targetChapters: 5, 7, 8, 11, 14, 17, 19
- id: MAP-DC3A63D407
- assessment: designed
- contractDisposition: retained
- contractRationale: Durable draft revision and CAS are effect-command semantics; staging is not a reason to expose a universal provider action set or to transactionize data queries.
- contractAnchors:
  - [K08](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K10](../composition-contract.md)
- sourceEvidence:
  - packages/uta-protocol/src/types/git.ts:104-110: AddResult is `{staged:true,index:number,operation:Operation}`.
  - services/uta/src/domain/trading/git/TradingGit.ts:77-91: add rejects in-flight/pending writes, pushes operation into in-memory staging, and returns index/operation.
- currentBehavior: Staging is process-memory state with array index; an operation is returned immediately before any durable command receipt or schema validation beyond caller construction.
- problem: Index is unstable across restart/concurrency and operation payload may be native/partial. No command ID, revision, digest, scope confirmation, or durable draft exists.
- targetModel: Replace with `DraftRevisionView { transactionId; revision; commandId; actionRef; action: TradeAction; scope; payloadDigest; createdAt; status }` returned only from a writer receipt. `ReplaceDraft` is an explicit command; actions are normalized/validated before staging and can be reloaded.
- pureTransitions:
  - createDraft(commandId, actionInput, facts) -&gt; Result&lt;DraftRevision, DomainFailure&gt;.
  - replaceDraft(expectedRevision, commandId, actions) -&gt; Result&lt;DraftRevision, VersionConflict|DomainFailure&gt;.
  - idempotent(commandId,digest) -&gt; original receipt | IdempotencyConflict.
- effectBoundary: Application receives input; writer atomically validates and stores durable draft/revision. No array index or local mutation is protocol authority.
- durability: Persist command receipt, revision, action payload, scope, digest, and event atomically. A returned receipt means commit succeeded; client cancellation does not roll back draft.
- errors:
  - IdempotencyConflict -&gt; return original/typed conflict.
  - VersionConflict -&gt; reload current revision.
  - OrderValidation/ScopeFailure -&gt; no draft event.
  - StorageUnavailable -&gt; no staged success.
- preservedBehavior:
  - Preserve user staging workflow and index-like ordering only as presentation ordinal.
  - Correct volatile array and native operation return with durable revision/receipt.
- replacementSteps:
  - Migrate stage endpoints/clients to transaction draft command.
  - Remove in-memory staging array from authority path.
  - Expose ordinal as projection only, not identity.
- verificationCases:
  - Restart after add and observe draft remains available.
  - Submit same command twice and observe one receipt.
  - Replace stale revision and observe VersionConflict without losing current draft.
- openQuestions: —
- review: accepted — Accepted: git.ts:104-110 returns an in-memory array index/operation, and TradingGit.ts:77-91 rejects or appends volatile staging. The final DraftRevisionView is a normalized, scope-bound writer receipt with command/digest/revision and explicit ReplaceDraft/CAS, so restart and concurrency cannot reinterpret an array index (MAP-DC3A63D407; K02/K03/K08/K11).

  - DecodeFailure -&gt; DispatchFailure/ProtocolViolation.
  - UnknownAfterSend -&gt; Reconciling/RecoveryRequired.

  - Reject after DispatchStarted and observe Abort/RecoveryRequired, not fake user-rejected order.
  - Retry same command ID returns same receipt.

- review: accepted — Accepted: git.ts:127-131 and TradingGit.ts:187-238 represent user reject as a synthetic commit with old hash/count and snapshot. The final no-effects rejection response carries transaction/revision/actor/CAS evidence, releases locks atomically, creates no broker job, and refuses invalid post-dispatch rejection (MAP-FC6B6B08DC; K02/K08/K10/K11).

### MAP-FE024081BB

- mapping source: [packages/uta-protocol/src/types/broker.ts:170-180](../../../../packages/uta-protocol/src/types/broker.ts#L170-L180)
- symbol: PlaceOrderResult
- unique targetChapters: 1, 4, 5, 9, 12, 14, 19
- id: MAP-FE024081BB
- assessment: designed
- contractDisposition: reframed
- contractRationale: The contradictory success bag is replaced at the effect boundary by action-associated acknowledgement and observation schemas, not one universal mutation result.
- contractAnchors:
  - [K03](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K07](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K08](../composition-contract.md)
- sourceEvidence:
  - packages/uta-protocol/src/types/broker.ts:170-180: PlaceOrderResult combines success boolean, optional orderId/error/message, native Execution/OrderState, and optional bracket legs for place/modify/close.
- currentBehavior: All three mutations return the same bag; callers infer action outcome from success and optional fields and often catch Error separately.
- problem: The bag permits contradictory states (success without identity, error with execution, close result shaped like place), loses acknowledgement versus observation, and cannot model unknown post-send outcomes or FailurePolicy.
- targetModel: Replace it with descriptor-bound `DispatchAcknowledgement&lt;LeafAction&gt;` and `RemoteOutcome&lt;LeafResult&gt;` schemas selected from the provider leaf: acknowledgement says accepted/received plus the exact scoped identity declared by that leaf; observation is the leaf’s typed outcome, which may distinguish Confirmed/Rejected/StillWorking/Unknown. Attach `DispatchFailure`, provider-declared rejection variants, and leg graph only where valid.
- pureTransitions:
  - compileAction(action, facts) -&gt; Result&lt;PreparedStep, PrepareFailure&gt;; action tag is retained.
  - dispatch(preparedStep, DispatchIdentity) -&gt; Result&lt;Ack&lt;LeafAction&gt;, DispatchFailure&gt;; never returns Filled by implication.
  - observe(attempt, typedObservation) -&gt; RemoteOutcome&lt;LeafResult&gt;; criterion evaluator decides settlement.
- effectBoundary: BrokerActionInterpreter owns native IO and maps raw responses; journal writer/application owns durable acknowledgement/progress. Protocol only encodes serializable associated variants.
- durability: Persist DispatchStarted before mutation, then scoped ack/observation with attempt epoch and evidence. Do not write success boolean or generic error string as authority.
- errors:
  - ActionMismatch -&gt; ProtocolViolation/defect.
  - DispatchUnknown(identity) -&gt; Reconciling/ObserveUnknown, no blind resend.
  - BrokerRejected(reason) -&gt; FailurePolicy decision; not generic Error.
  - LegObservationMissing -&gt; partial outcome.
- preservedBehavior:
  - Preserve immediate fill details where native evidence exists, but represent them as observation facts rather than success semantics.
  - Correct unified result contract so modify/cancel/close cannot accidentally be interpreted as place.
- replacementSteps:
  - Create action-specific codecs and interpreter result types.
  - Migrate TradingGit.parseOperationResult and callers to typed outcome adapters.
  - Remove `success/error/message` bag after projections consume typed records.
- verificationCases:
  - Ack without fill leaves order Working under AcceptedByVenue criterion.
  - Network timeout after DispatchStarted yields Unknown and durable observation job.
  - Cancel response with no final status is Pending/StillWorking, not cancelled.
- openQuestions: —
- review: accepted — Accepted after repair: broker.ts:170-180 uses one success/error/native-state bag for place, modify, and close, allowing contradictory payloads. The final target binds DispatchAcknowledgement and RemoteOutcome to the selected leaf and keeps unknown-after-send, provider rejection, and leg data only where declared, rather than treating a boolean as execution authority (MAP-FE024081BB; K02/K03/K07/K08/K11).
- design: [design.md](design.md)

### MAP-FEF9B7F5AE

- mapping source: [packages/uta-protocol/src/types/git.ts:79-89](../../../../packages/uta-protocol/src/types/git.ts#L79-L89)
- symbol: GitState
- unique targetChapters: 6, 7, 10, 11, 14, 17, 19
- id: MAP-FEF9B7F5AE
- assessment: designed
- contractDisposition: reframed
- contractRationale: GitState remains a projection of normalized account/order observations; its rebuild and legacy rules must not drag provider SDK objects or transaction approval into reads.
- contractAnchors:
  - [K03](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K05](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K08](../composition-contract.md)
  - [K11](../composition-contract.md)
- sourceEvidence:
  - packages/uta-protocol/src/types/git.ts:79-89: GitState stores string account totals plus arrays of Position and OpenOrder.
  - services/uta/src/domain/trading/git/TradingGit.ts:632-645: rehydrateGitState wraps quantities in Decimal and fills missing multiplier with 1 for older commits.
- currentBehavior: A post-commit snapshot is persisted inside each GitCommit, with mutable/native broker-shaped positions/orders; rehydration applies ad hoc Decimal/default logic.
- problem: The snapshot mixes execution audit and read projection, lacks scope/sequence/freshness/valuation uncertainty, and a missing multiplier default may conceal legacy evidence. Rebuilds depend on broker protocol types.
- targetModel: Replace with `AccountProjectionSnapshot { scope; accounting: Money/ValuationView; positions: PositionObservation[]; orders: OrderView[]; sourceSequence; asOf; freshness; valuationEvidence }`. Snapshot is rebuildable from journal/projection checkpoints; legacy missing fields are tagged LegacyEvidence, not silently normalized for writes.
- pureTransitions:
  - foldAccounting(events, observations) -&gt; ProjectionSnapshot; pure and versioned.
  - validateSnapshot(snapshot) -&gt; Result&lt;ValidProjection, ProjectionViolation&gt;; sequence/hash/freshness checked.
  - importLegacyGitState(record) -&gt; ReadOnlyLegacyProjection | MigratedSnapshot only with evidence.
- effectBoundary: Projection store reads/writes snapshots; journal is authority. Broker SDK/Decimal not needed to rebuild normalized views.
- durability: Persist projection checkpoint sequence/schema version and source journal hash atomically. `GitState` export carries read cursor/freshness, not executable state.
- errors:
  - ProjectionSequenceGap -&gt; rebuild required.
  - LegacyMissingScope/Multiplier -&gt; LegacyEvidence and write block.
  - ValuationUncertain -&gt; explicit status, not zero/default.
  - NativePayload -&gt; decode failure.
- preservedBehavior:
  - Preserve account totals, positions, pending orders as a trader-facing view.
  - Preserve multiplier-aware arithmetic but make legacy fallback evidence explicit.
  - Correct embedding native values in Git commit.
- replacementSteps:
  - Create accounting/order projection schemas and checkpoint rebuild.
  - Migrate Git show/export to read projection.
  - Delete GitState as execution input and remove ad hoc rehydrate defaults.
- verificationCases:
  - Rebuild snapshot with a skipped journal event and observe sequence gap.
  - Read mixed-currency snapshot and observe valuation uncertainty.
  - Load legacy no-multiplier state and observe read-only evidence.
- openQuestions: —
- review: accepted — Accepted: git.ts:79-89 embeds mutable Position/OpenOrder arrays in GitState, and TradingGit.ts:632-645 rehydrates Decimal while defaulting missing multiplier to 1. The final scoped projection snapshot is journal-rebuildable and marks missing identity/multiplier as LegacyEvidence/uncertainty, never as executable normalized state (MAP-FEF9B7F5AE; K02/K03/K05/K07/K08/K11).

## Cross-group contracts

- AccountScope is required on account-bound controlled effects, order/position observations, conflict keys and account-authenticated market observations; public Candle/Instrument/News data uses an explicit PublicMarket source variant or a provider-declared scope and never receives a default account. Evidence: UnifiedTradingAccount.ts:642-688, :700-724, :759-790 and git.ts:256-305.
- CapabilityDescriptor is the fixed UTA-facing envelope (identity/path, schema versions/fingerprint, input/result/error schemas, delivery/effect/resource metadata, provenance and availability); provider capability trees are open, leaves may be absent, and an existing leaf can be unavailable without becoming structural absence. There is no global ActionContractMap or mandatory full Broker SDK. Evidence: broker.ts:475-620.
- Order is a semantic unit and controlled-effect input composed by provider declarations/HOFs. Units versus Notional, amount versus percent, timing and protection remain local validated relations; native MOC/LOC/REL/OPG or other fields survive as exact provider extensions. No provider is required to accept another provider’s leaf, and native atomicity is never inferred from shape. Evidence: UnifiedTradingAccount.ts:603-637, :703-724 and cited IBKR/Alpaca/Longbridge/CCXT sources.
- RuntimeHealth is a closed process observation ADT; broker reach, capability availability, authorization and transaction admission are separate. Health observations never grant dispatch permission. Evidence: broker.ts:366-426.
- Pull results are finite data projections and push streams have explicit frame/lifecycle/cursor/backpressure contracts. Complete/Partial/Unavailable and freshness/finality remain explicit; data reads and caches do not use prepare/approve/compensate or per-frame transaction WAL. Evidence: broker.ts:322-364, :428-450.
- JournalWriter/events/attempts are authority only for controlled effects; Git/history/manager and market-data outputs are rebuildable projections. DispatchStarted is durable before remote mutation, and response/storage loss remains Unknown/RecoveryRequired. Evidence: TradingGit.ts:141-185, :160-180, :171-180.
- InstrumentId/InstrumentDescriptor/ScopedOrderRef and PositionObservation are normalized identities/facts; native Contract/Order/Decimal stay adapter-local. A string aliceId, symbol or branded string alone cannot prove equality. Evidence: contract-ext.ts:4-22, :25-31 and broker.ts:10-12.
- Protocol failures are route/leaf/action-associated ADTs with redacted evidence and typed recovery (ProtocolViolation, QueryFailure, CapabilityFailure, BrokerRejection, DispatchUnknown, StorageUnavailable); WireBrokerError and Error.message are not a universal contract. Evidence: broker.ts:44-79 and errors.ts:10-18.

## Additional findings

- services/uta/src/domain/trading/UnifiedTradingAccount.ts:603-637 validates MKT Units versus cashQty Notional, requires prices by order type, and distinguishes TRAIL from TRAIL LIMIT with mutually exclusive auxPrice/trailingPercent; any provider-declared order leaf must preserve these relations before native compilation; the allowed sizing/kind combinations remain provider-specific.
- services/uta/src/domain/trading/UnifiedTradingAccount.ts:642-688 memoizes broker subaccounts, treats an absent/empty listing (including not-yet-probed) as one implicit default, and only then validates requested wallet against instrument routing; directory discovery must instead expose Discovering/Available/Unavailable and never infer execution scope.
- services/uta/src/domain/trading/UnifiedTradingAccount.ts:776-790 clears staged subaccount IDs after commit and persists them only by appending a [sub:...] message tag; operation/action payloads and durable conflict keys therefore need an explicit AccountScope migration rather than message parsing.
- services/uta/src/domain/trading/git/TradingGit.ts:141-185 executes each operation and only afterward snapshots state, appends/persists GitCommit, and clears staging; a remote side effect can precede persistence failure, so the controlled-effect wrapper must write DispatchStarted and attempt identity before adapter mutation and classify response loss as Unknown.
- services/uta/src/domain/trading/git/TradingGit.ts:546-560 strips IBKR sentinels with OrderHelper but casts the result back to Order/Partial&lt;Order&gt;; this is a concrete unsafe serialization path even though comments claim native Orders never leave the class, requiring exact provider-declared input/observation codecs and no cast-based projection.
- services/uta/src/domain/trading/git/TradingGit.ts:579-645 rehydrates Decimal fields and fills missing Position.multiplier with 1 for old commit files; legacy import must retain a LegacyEvidence marker and only construct PositionObservation after identity/unit validation, not silently bless the default for writes.
- services/uta/src/domain/trading/order-history.ts:101-124 omits unknown cancel rows and casts sync result statuses directly into OrderHistoryStatus; the new history reducer must retain an audit event with explicit association and represent unknown/partial/reconciling lifecycle instead of dropping or casting it.
- services/uta/src/domain/trading/uta-manager.ts:205-295 converts missing account info to USD/zero rows and filters failed/empty contract-search groups; manager projections need structured valuation/completeness states so offline, partial, no-match, and keyless cases remain distinguishable.
- services/uta/src/domain/trading/contract-search.ts:44-64 uses Promise.allSettled but silently drops rejected account searches before flattening native descriptions; InstrumentSearchResponse must preserve per-scope Unavailable/Partial groups and catalog revision while still isolating one broker failure from others.
- services/uta/src/domain/trading/brokers/ibkr/IbkrBroker.ts:874-878 advertises MOC/LOC/REL, while packages/ibkr/src/order.ts:72-75 marks percentOffset REL-only; any provider-declared order leaf must retain offset relation evidence rather than impose a universal order-kind map.
- services/uta/src/domain/trading/brokers/alpaca/AlpacaBroker.ts:66-74 maps OPG to opg, LongbridgeBroker.ts:103-120 rejects OPG, and CcxtBroker.ts:509-611 does not include order.tif in place params; OpeningAuction therefore remains an explicit provider capability/parameter decision rather than raw TIF forwarding or default-Day fallback.
